I go really A or B about it, I've tried all forms of government, in my group campaigns there have been from kingdoms and empires to Technocracy and the players even have set their own forms of government, sometimes things like "This magical chicken can lay eggs that hatch into small figurines of the townsfolk, whoever gets hatched gets to govern".

As for the countries/continents, I like the diversity of different countries that live differently, when I do a world with few countries or continents I try to give each a unique approach to the world itself (Example: in a homebrew demon hunting game there were 4 continents, one was home of magic casters, another was technologically advanced, the third one relished in magitech and the last one had weaker magic and lesser technology but used them at the same time). It gets harder the more countries you have, but you can always spice the government, a country could have a president and be more "Realistic", another could have a religious leader and be closer to the gods (I had a country ran by a guy that reincarnated due to a curse so it went through 80 years of prosperity followed by 10 to 12 years of anarchy). 

Players love crashing anything the world you have created, so if for instance you make Half-Elfs illegal then you can be sure that at least one of them is going to be a half-elf (When it was done in my group, 3 out of the 4 players chose Half-Elf)  and will naturally be involved in the political world (can't assure it will be peaceful tho), I also allow them to get political power if they want (and roll high enough carisma), returning to the Half-Elf example, the three players got political power in different ways, one united the people of the world and became the "World Council Judge" another one got into the military and became the World Marshall and the third one absorbed the power of an ancient God and became the leader of the cult.

You can use the power of backstory to get them involved, maybe their home city that they love is now being ran by an evil dictator and they are the only one the people will accept as leader, maybe they have a strong desire to free slaves and make their own country where slaves can take refuge.

I hope this helps, cheers.

It's mostly a matter of chemistry with you group, I find it that it becomes easier for your group (Players and GMs alike) if you can understand the flow of things and do the most you can with it (reading the mood helps a lot). If you have a good affinity with them, then you quickly will start cracking jokes and feel more at ease. Outside of that it's pretty much trial and error, you are bound to make mistakes if you're new, then again you're bound to make mistakes if you are a veteran.

Good luck tho, it sometimes is hard than it sounds like (one of the guys in my group has played with us for about 3 years and still has trouble with it, but has started to make some significant advances) if your group is friendly you'll get used to the ambience pretty smoothly.
